title: A contract surface that is wrong for the language that reads it
description: Every numeric position here is one this checker refuses, so the red proof can break each one in isolation. Committed so a reviewer reads what is being broken rather than reconstructing it; the breakages are applied to COPIES of this file, never to the file in the tree.

snowflake_id.description: A 64-bit identifier declared as an integer with a maximum past the float64 exact range. A value at 2**53 + 1 is exact in Go, Python and Ruby and is already wrong in TypeScript, by one.

shard_id.description: A CLOSED SET of integers that includes 2**53 + 1. An enum is a stronger statement than a maximum rather than a weaker one — it enumerates the complete set of legal values, so this member is a value the contract requires and a JavaScript client cannot carry. Before core-numeric-enum-53-01 this field produced exactly one finding, a numeric.enum warning about evolution, and said nothing about the value.

byte_size.description: A byte count with NO maximum at all. Unbounded is only alarming where the ceiling is reachable, and an int64 file size can reach 2**53 — only the writer bounds it.

expires_at.description: A JWT `exp` claim with no maximum. Unbounded, and named like an identity.

status_code.description: A numeric enum. Codegen closes it into a union in all six languages at once, so adding a value is a breaking change in six of them.
